approved: Completion of Kakadu National Park (Koongarra Project Area Repeal) Bill 2013
Sustainability, Environment, Water, Population and Communities

Introduced a bill repealing the Koongarra Project Area Act to complete Kakadu National Park by incorporating the 1,288 hectares of Koongarra, at the request of traditional owner Jeffrey Lee, who declined mining offers worth millions of dollars, following Koongarra's inclusion in the Kakadu World Heritage area in June 2011.

Supported the Completion of Kakadu National Park (Koongarra Project Area Repeal) Bill 2013, saying traditional owners wanted Koongarra incorporated into Kakadu National Park, while noting Northern Territory concerns that existing domestic legislation already protected the area.

Supported the bill to incorporate Koongarra into Kakadu National Park, commending Jeffrey Lee's opposition to uranium mining and urging stronger scrutiny of the Ranger mine's environmental risks, while arguing Kakadu would remain incomplete until Ranger closed.

Supported the bill to restore Koongarra to Kakadu National Park, describing traditional owners' efforts to protect the area as significant and welcoming recent environmental decisions involving marine parks, the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area and the Murray-Darling.

Supported the bill to complete Kakadu National Park, acknowledging traditional owners and the roles of Jeffrey Lee and Bob Hawke, while highlighting the government's environmental initiatives, including the Coral Sea marine park and plans for the Murray-Darling Basin.

Explained that the bill repeals the Koongarra Project Area Act 1981 to prevent future mining and incorporate Koongarra into Kakadu National Park, in accordance with Jeffrey Lee's expressed views and the government's 2010 election commitment.
Announced that the bill would complete Kakadu National Park by removing any future option for uranium mining, and said the decision respected Jeffrey Lee's wish for his land to be protected forever.
